## Observation
During a compaction fold, `_build_authorship_ledger` -> `authorship.identify_signer` -> `_keyring_for` -> `rebar.show_ticket` -> `ensure_fresh` runs while `_compact_locked` holds the store write lock. When the 60 s freshness marker has expired, `ensure_fresh` runs `git fetch` (network in production) and then `sync.reconverge`, which requests the same store write lock the fold already holds. It waits out its 2 s pass against its own process, then gives up.

Measured on a clone of `tickets` at `daa3a65239b^` with a local mirror as `origin` (2026-11-03, `origin/main` `25bce6c0550`): first signed fold `ensure_fresh` 2.22 s, nested lock wait 2.04 s, fetch 0.11 s (local mirror; production fetches over the network). Evidence on `breezelike-travelsick-moray`.

## Expected
A locked critical section never fetches and never requests a lock it already holds. Keyring lookups for the ledger read local state, or run before the lock like `preresolve_unmapped_positions`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A fold with signed events runs no `git fetch` and no store-lock acquisition while `_compact_locked` holds the lock (test observes the lock dir at each call: `test_no_fetch_or_nested_lock_request_while_the_fold_holds_the_lock` in `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py`).
- [x] The authorship ledger is unchanged for the same input (`test_presolved_signers_leave_the_ledger_unchanged` in `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py`).
